context: Force-layout network diagram with 50 nodes and ~110 edges, six communities distinguished by redundant color+texture encoding (Tol bright palette + SVG patterns: hatch, dots, crosshatch, horizontal, waves, vertical), with a grayscale toggle to verify texture alone carries community structure.
first_impression: The six communities are largely readable at a glance — cluster pull keeps them spatially separated and the dual-encoding (color + texture) reinforces group membership without competing channels.
what_works: Redundant encoding is well-executed: the six distinct textures (diagonal hatch, dots, crosshatch, horizontal stripes, waves, vertical stripes) are perceptually diverse enough to work in grayscale mode, validating the pedagogical point. Hover-to-highlight neighborhood interaction reduces edge clutter on demand, and the compact legend with matching swatches maps cleanly to both channels.
what_doesnt: Alpha (blue, diagonal hatch) and Zeta (purple, vertical) nodes intermix on the left side of the layout, weakening the spatial cluster separation that the design depends on — a viewer must lean on texture or color rather than position to distinguish these two communities. Epsilon (light blue, waves) scatters into isolated satellite nodes far from its cluster centroid, making its community boundary ambiguous without hovering.
